transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here about my sleep, mostly. It's just... it's been broken for a long time now. I fall into bed exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm just awake before the alarm even goes off. I feel like I never really rested.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things that usually make you happy?

I guess so. It's... well, most days it just feels like the color has gone out of things. Um... even when I'm just sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, or... looking at art I used to enjoy. I just... I have to work pretty hard not to tear up. For no clear reason.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried specifically about not being able to sleep well?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I get anxious about it. It's just... kind of how it is now. I don't really sit there worrying over it.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or do you feel more fatigued than usual, even after trying to rest?

Um... yes. I guess I'm tired a lot. After I finish seeing my home-health clients and... come back to help at home... my body just feels heavy. Just... even doing my charting notes or folding laundry... it can feel like too much to push through.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?
Um... I don't really think so. I still try to see my friends sometimes and... do things. I just... I don't know.
Do you feel that your mood has been consistently low, even when your sleep is better than usual?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. It doesn't really matter how I sleep. Most days just... feel like the color has gone out of things. Even if I'm just sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, or... looking at art I used to like... I just... I have to work pretty hard not to tear up. And there's no clear reason for it. It's just how it is.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not worth much or that you're letting people down, even when there's no real reason for it?
Um... no, not really. I don't think so. I mean... I do my job, and I help out at home, so... I don't feel like I'm letting anyone down. I just... no. I don't have thoughts like that.
Has your mood felt low or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Um... yes. I think I just said that a minute ago. It's most days. Like I mentioned... the color is just gone from everything. Even if I'm sitting at Sunday dinner, or trying to look at art... it's like that all day. I just... I have to try hard not to cry, and there's no real reason for it.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy don’t bring you any pleasure anymore—even things like seeing friends, hobbies, or activities you’ve always liked?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I've stopped enjoying things. I still go to work, and I still... I still like being with my family. It's just... I just feel down while I'm doing them. But I still like them.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately, even when you're trying to do something simple like reading or making decisions?
Um... no. I don't think so. I can still read just fine. And making decisions... well, I just make them. I haven't really noticed any trouble with that.
Can you think of something you used to really enjoy—like a hobby, a TV show, or time with a friend—and tell me how it feels when you do it now? Do you still get the same pleasure from it?

Um... I don't know. Like I said, I still enjoy things. I still watch TV and see my family. It's... it's just the same. I just feel sad while I'm doing it. But the things themselves... they haven't changed.
Can you think of something you used to really enjoy—like a hobby, a TV show, or time with a friend—and tell me how it feels when you do it now? Do you still get the same pleasure from it?

I... I think you just asked me that. Like I said, I don't really have a different answer for it. I still get pleasure from things. I just happen to feel low while I'm doing them. I don't really know what else to say about it.

Can you think of something you used to really look forward to—like a hobby, an event, or time with someone—and tell me what it feels like when you do it now? Do you still feel that sense of anticipation or enjoyment, or does it feel different somehow?

I... I feel like we're just going in circles here. I mean, you keep asking me the same thing. I don't know what you want me to say. I still look forward to seeing my grandkids. I still like my shows. It's not the things that are different. I just... I just have this heavy feeling all the time. That's all.

When you spend time with your grandkids or watch your favorite shows, do you still feel the same joy or pleasure you used to feel, or does it feel more like a habit or something you just go through the motions with?
I... I don't know. It's just normal. I watch them, I see the kids. It's... I don't think about it like that. I just do it.
When you're with your grandkids or watching your favorite shows, do you find that you don't enjoy them as much as you used to, even if you still do them?
No. I... I enjoy them the same. It's not that I don't like doing those things anymore. I just... I don't really know how else to explain it to you.

When you're doing things you used to really enjoy, like seeing your grandkids or watching your favorite shows, do you still feel the same pleasure or happiness you used to, or does it feel like you're just going through the motions?
I just... I just told you. It's the same. I still like them. I don't... I don't know why you keep asking me this.
When you're with your grandkids or watching your favorite shows, do you feel the same level of happiness you used to, or has it become more of a routine without really feeling happy inside?
Look... I feel happy. It's not just a routine. I really don't have a different answer for you.
Do you often wake up much earlier than you intend to, and then have trouble falling back asleep?
Yeah... my sleep is pretty broken. Has been for a long time now. I fall into bed exhausted, but then I end up waking up before my alarm goes off. I just... I never really feel like I rested.

When you're doing things you used to really enjoy, like seeing your grandkids or watching your favorite shows, do you still feel the same pleasure or happiness you used to, or does it feel like you're just going through the motions?
Didn't you... didn't you just ask me that? We just talked about this. I still enjoy seeing them. I don't know what else to tell you.
